title: A finite algebra over a henselian local ring is a product of henselian local rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and $R\to B$ a ring map making $B$ a finitely generated $R$-module. Then there are an integer $r\ge0$, local rings $(B_1,\mathfrak n_1),\dots,(B_r,\mathfrak n_r)$, each an $R$-algebra and a finitely generated $R$-module, and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $B\cong B_1\times\dots\times B_r$ ($B=0$ if $r=0$), such that for every $i$: $B_i$ is a henselian local ring, and $R\to B_i$ is a local homomorphism ($\mathfrak n_i\cap R=\mathfrak m$, the preimage of $\mathfrak n_i$ in $R$ being $\mathfrak m$), so that $B_i/\mathfrak n_i$ is a finite field extension of $\kappa$ [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GH (lemma-finite-over-henselian) (1) and (2), and its proof: '(2) implies (1) since S as in (1) is a finite product of its localizations at the primes lying over m by Lemma 04GG (10); (2) also follows from 04GG (10) since any finite S-algebra is also a finite R-algebra (any finite ring map between local rings is local)'

proof.text: Apply henselian etale retraction to the test algebras after lifting the base with ULift into their universe. Transport the residue-field isomorphism across ULift. The finite-algebra product-local theorem then gives B as an R-algebra product of local rings A_i.

Transfer module finiteness along the product algebra equivalence; each component is module-finite by the surjective projection. Integral contraction of each maximal ideal gives the local structure map.
Apply the finite-local-algebra henselianity lemma to every local factor A_i.

For each factor, Mathlib IsLocalRing.ResidueField.finite_of_module_finite gives finiteness of the residue-field algebra from the local structure map and Module.Finite R A_i. Package the decomposition and all component properties. The empty product includes B=0.
